lead: Winding streets on a mountainside: the neighbourhood that built itself.
text: Its name comes from two towers built by the Pinós family between the 16th and 18th centuries. In the early 20th century a garden city was planned here, but it failed because of its remote location, and after the Civil War the sale of cheap land attracted immigrants in the 1950s and 1960s, who built their own houses.

It keeps a singular character, with winding streets that follow the terrain and Avinguda de Vallbona as the road linking it to the rest of Nou Barris. In 1978, Manolo Vital "hijacked" a line 47 bus to demand public transport, a gesture that sums up the history of effort of its residents. At 1,739 €/m², it is among the neighbourhoods with the lowest sale price in Barcelona.
housing: Self-built homes on winding mountain streets.
